title: Name the docket's own quest and event prerequisites on the LISTING (the scene-level half of eca7893d8b0be480)
body:
`533a233c` built the option-level half of the listing hint and is **inert on the shipped docket**. The docket's gates are declared at SCENE level, so the listing still says nothing in exactly the state all six players were in.

## Verified against the shipped content and the code

`content/world/new_york_overworld.json` declares "Rowan's Winter Return Docket" (`albany_city__civic_core__job`) with its prerequisites on the authored SCENE, not on the options:

    requires_completed_quests: [wolf_winter]
    requires_resolved_events:  [albany_city__civic_core__event]

`localJobSceneListingBlockedReason` (src/world/local_job_scene.ts) opens with

    if (!localJobSceneRequirementsMet(scene, state)) return null;

and `localJobSceneRequirementsMet` is precisely the check over `requires_completed_quests`, `requires_resolved_events` and the scene-level world facts. So whenever a scene-level gate is unmet the listing hint is `null` by design — which is the correct shape for the option-level work `533a233c` did, and leaves the docket untouched.

All six refusals happened with Wolf-Winter incomplete, i.e. the scene gate unmet. On the real docket, today, the listing is still silent. `533a233c`'s own "honest scope" paragraph says the same thing; this item is the half it deliberately left.

## A second finding, not in the original plan

The scene-level REJECTION already exists and already names the gate — but in engine ids, not player terms (src/world/session_local_actions.ts):

    Complete quest "wolf_winter" before working Rowan's Winter Return Docket.
    Resolve event "albany_city__civic_core__event" before working ...

So this is not purely additive on the listing side. `wolf_winter` and `albany_city__civic_core__event` are not things a player can look up; the quest is "Wolf-Winter" and the event is the Albany Civic Center charter backlog. Both surfaces need to speak in titles, and the rejection's current wording is part of what has to change — otherwise parity would be achieved by making the listing as unhelpful as the rejection.

## What a player actually saw, verbatim

On build `5afc7531` (seed 1788725013, wave 4) the refusal a player received was, word for word:

    Complete quest "wolf_winter" before working Rowan's Winter Return Docket.

That single line contains the whole item. The scene-level rejection DOES name the gate — and names it as `wolf_winter`, an engine id the player cannot look up, rather than "Wolf-Winter". The listing, meanwhile, said nothing at all. That player went on to complete Wolf-Winter later in the same run and never retried the docket, and filed the experience as:

> job availability gating only discovered by trying and getting rejected

which is the defect stated better than any of our own summaries: the information exists, and it is only reachable by failing.

## The change

When a DISCOVERED job's scene-level chronology gate is unmet, the listing's blocked reason carries the same text as the scene-level rejection — "complete <quest title>", "resolve <event title>" — in player terms, produced by ONE shared helper, so listing/rejection parity holds for scene-level gates exactly as `533a233c` established it for option-level ones.

Undiscovered jobs and `hiddenJobCount` semantics are unchanged: this is about a job the player can already see and cannot act on, not about revealing anything.

Keep `533a233c`'s existing judgement rather than re-deriving it: an option foreclosed by a contradictory one-time decision is excluded from the hint, and when everything is foreclosed the surface says nothing. A hint that told a player to resolve an event they had already resolved the other way would be worse than the silence this item is about.

## Acceptance

1. A test drives the REAL docket scene from shipped content, in the six players' actual state — POI scouted, contact talked, Wolf-Winter incomplete, charter-backlog event unresolved — through BOTH surfaces, and asserts the listing names Wolf-Winter (and the charter-backlog filing while it is unresolved) and the rejection returns the identical string. Driving the real content is the point: the option-level work passed its tests and was still inert on the actual docket, because the tests exercised fixtures rather than the shipped scene.
2. The parity test from `533a233c` is extended to scene-level gates.
3. Legend/version pins move once, deliberately — inspected and stated, not blindly re-pinned.
4. Titles, never ids, on BOTH surfaces — the quest by its title, the event by its title. The parity test asserts the listing string EQUALS the rejection string for the real docket in that state, so parity cannot be satisfied by leaving both of them unhelpful.

On landing, close `eca7893d8b0be480` with the sha. `56b3d1a6260af50c` is already done.

## Cross-references

- `intake/queue` P1 `eca7893d8b0be480` — the parent, open since the refusal half landed.
- `intake/queue` P1 `83fc32b6e9e9f715` — the listing item `533a233c` answered at option level.
- `533a233c` — the option-level listing hint, correct and inert here.
- `bc5de6e9` / `traces/bugs/bug_0624_job_event_empty_option_gate_unnamed.yaml` — the refusal half.

evidence.summary: 533a233c is inert on the shipped docket: its listing hint returns null whenever a SCENE-level gate is unmet, and the docket's gates are scene-level. All six refusals were in exactly that state.
